newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open lower on franc, strike worries.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open lower on franc, strike worries.

text.p: French shares opened lower, ignoring gains on Wall Street and other European markets, due to renewed pressure on the franc and growing worries about possible strike action in the autumn, dealers said.

The shares were also affected by a slippage in bond prices due to lower than expected June industrial production, showing the economy is still faltering. CGT-union leader Marc Blondel is due to hold a news conference today and investors are eager to get clues about the union's attitude towards possible strikes.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 4.05 points or 0.2 percent at 2,013.94 at 0815 GMT.
The CAC future was down 4.5 at 2,016.

A poll in the La Tribune Desfosses newspaper reported that 77 percent of those asked expect tough strike action this autumn, 62 percent will sustain consumer purchases and 35 percent plan to cut their consumption.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe is set to unveil on September 10 the outlines of the 1997 austerity budget, a fiscal reform and a financing plan for the social security system.
As public sector unions prepare their response to planned budget cuts, Nicole Notat, head of the country's largest union, the CFDT, warned on Tuesday of "tension and conflicts".
France's 1996 welfare deficit is likely to exceed 50 billion francs, about three times the amount originally predicted by the government, according to press reports.
The equities market is also bracing itself for a series of first half results by major companies such as BNP, Elf Aquitaine, Total, Casino and Danone due next week.
